cases.citation: plutiedev vdp-commands (VRAM write command, data-port writes land at consecutive auto-increment addresses); Sega documentation (the write FIFO preserves order). Eight words 0x1111..0x8888 written to VRAM 0x1000 read back in that order

Sega documentation (status bit 8 = write FIFO full; four entries); gendev t=851 Nemesis VRAM-access measurements (the VDP accepts a data-port word only at an external-access slot, 16 per active H32 line, so back-to-back 68000 writes fill the FIFO and stall the CPU). The status read immediately follows a sustained eight-word burst in active display; only bit 8 is judged
Sega documentation (status bit 9 = write FIFO empty, bit 8 = full): after polling until bit 9 reads set, the FIFO is empty and not full

gendev t=851 Nemesis VRAM-access measurements (external-access slots per line: 16 active versus 166 blank for H32, so blanking drains far faster than active display); the same eight-word burst with the display off leaves bit 8 (FIFO full) clear

Sega documentation (each FIFO entry carries its own address and data): two words written at VRAM 0x1200 and 0x1202 are not redirected by a new VRAM address command issued while they are queued; the word written after the command lands at 0x1300

Number of guest instructions before the full flag first reads set depends on Genewhip instruction timing and the unmeasured slot schedule; observed bytes are reported only (twelve status words, one after each write)
ROM control flow reached the final store (no stop before the last wait)
